Mirae Asset Securities Research | May 26, 2025

Mirae Asset Securities Research2 | Mirae Asset Minutes
Top stories
• The cosmetics sector delivered stronger-
than-expected 1Q25 results. A key highlight 
was improving earnings in China (where 
expectations had been low). With earnings 
momentum building, valuations are 
recovering.
• Our top pick is Cosmax. Earnings growth 
should accelerate, as the firm has secured 
high-volume buyers and completed its 
capacity expansion ahead of schedule. 
Subsidiaries Cosmax Neo (packaging) and 
CM Tech (raw materials) are also reporting 
sharp earnings growth. 
• The China business (which accounts for 
around 30% of total revenue) is improving. 
In 1Q25, China revenue (consolidated) grew 
for the second consecutive quarter, and the 
Shanghai subsidiary returned to growth for 
the first time in four quarters. 
• The entertainment sector’s recent rally is 
likely to continue in 2H25, driven by 
improving earnings momentum. Notably, 
North American momentum is picking up 
again, and structural growth in merchandise 
sales is also encouraging. There is also 
growing optimism about the reopening of 
China’s concert market.
• Our top pick is SM Entertainment (TP: 
W160,000). In 2Q25, the consolidation of 
Dear U and comebacks by fast-rising groups 
(Aespa, Riize, and NCT Wish) should lead to 
record quarterly earnings and a valuation 
boost. Over the longer horizon, major 
groups are likely to increase their earnings 
contributions by increasingly tapping into 
the US market.
Top picks
Hyundai RotemHD HHI Hyosung HeavySamsung Biologics New PharmaResearch
• Pharma/biotech stocks have been weighed 
down by negative developments in the US 
(e.g., tariff risks and an executive order 
aimed at reducing drug prices)
• However, the impact on Samsung Biologics
should be limited. Tariffs should have a 
minimal effect on drug substance (DS) 
exports (given the small DS contribution to 
drug prices), while price reforms mainly 
target high-priced drugs (not biosimilars). In 
fact, moves to enhance cost efficiency could 
boost CDMO demand, benefiting the firm.
• The spin-off of the biosimilar business 
should help ease the stock’s valuation 
discount and eliminate concerns about 
conflicts of interest. We continue to present 
Samsung Biologics as our top pick.

Mirae Asset Securities Research3 | Mirae Asset Minutes
Investment ideas
• For our top 10 picks, we added Samsung Biologics, Cosmax, and SM Entertainment. We removed Samsung Electronics (SEC) and Hanwha Solutions due 
to growing uncertainty around US trade and subsidy policies, and we removed HYBE due to a change in our medium -term sector top pick. 
• For Samsung Biologics, we believe the planned spin-off of the biosimilar business has increased valuation upside, and we also ex pect the CDMO 
business to benefit from Trump’s executive order aimed at lowering drug prices. For Cosmax, we see strong earnings upside dri ven by improving results 
in China and faster-than-expected capacity expansion. Meanwhile, SM Entertainment stands to benefit from a sector -wide valuation re-rating along with 
multiple high-profile artist comebacks.
• While shares of PharmaResearch and Hyosung Heavy Industries have continued to climb (raising some valuation concerns), we believe their strong 
earnings outlooks justify their continued inclusion in our top picks list.  We also remain positive on HD Hyundai Heavy Indus tries (HD HHI) despite its 
recent weakness, as LNG carrier deliveries scheduled for 2Q -3Q25 should drive profit improvement. Recent news regarding rising g lobal naval ship 
demand is also positive for the stock. For Hyundai Rotem, we see ample upside to earnings amid increased global defense spend ing. 
Top 10 picks: Changes and comments
• Following the US-China agreement in Geneva (May 10–11), recession fears eased, and global equity markets rebounded quickly.
• However, key underlying issues remain unresolved, and the 30% tariff rate on Chinese imports, while reduced, is still substantial. With US stagflation 
risks lingering, further Fed rate cuts are likely to be delayed for an extended period.
• With margin pressure mounting, US big tech stocks may continue to experience muted momentum and downside pressure. While smal ler-cap names in 
certain sectors (e.g., nuclear power) may outperform due to policy tailwinds, the challenges facing the broader tech sector p oint to downside risk for the 
overall US equity market. 
• In Korea, we recommend reducing exposure to highly cyclical sectors/companies and those that are sensitive to tariff -related uncertainty. As a core 
strategy, we continue to favor the defense, shipbuilding, and beauty tech sectors. We also see opportunities in areas that co uld benefit from domestic 
economic stimulus and a recovery in China demand. 
• Meanwhile, at the May MPB meeting, the BOK is likely to cut the base rate by 25bps and could hint at further cuts to come. The won has r ecently 
strengthened to an appropriate level; considering current export conditions, we are cautious on the likelihood of further app reciation.
Lingering
 US stagflation risk; reduce exposure to cyclicals
Mirae Asset Securities Research4 | Mirae Asset Minutes
• Global pharma/biotech sentiment has weakened due to negative developments in the US, including: 1) proposals to ease regulati ons on 
domestic drug manufacturing and impose tariffs on drug imports; 2) the selection of a less biotech-friendly leader for the FDA’s Center for 
Biologics Evaluation and Research (CBER); 3) an executive order aimed at lowering drug prices; and 4) a draft plan for Medica re drug price 
negotiations. This has led to a broad decline across major Korean pharma stocks, with some exceptions (e.g., obesity-related stocks).
• However, as the proposed drug pricing reforms mainly target high-priced drugs, the impact on Samsung Biologics (which focuses on
biosimilars) should be minimal. In fact, we could see an increase in CDMO demand, which would benefit the company.
• Tariff concerns also look somewhat excessive. In particular, the impact on DS exporters such as Samsung Biologics and Daewoon g 
Pharmaceutical should be minimal, as customers are likely to absorb cost increases. (The DS share of total drug prices is onl y around 5%.)
Pharma/Biotech | Seung-min Kim   sm.kim.a@miraeasset.com

Mirae Asset Securities Research5 | Mirae Asset Minutes
• Samsung Biologics plans to spin off a holding company to oversee the biosimilar business while devoting itself fully to the C DMO business. 
This move should help eliminate concerns about conflicts of interest, strengthening its competitiveness in securing CDMO orde rs. It is also 
positive for consolidated results, given that Samsung Bioepis has been reporting lower growth and margins than the standalone business. 
• The new entity (tentatively named Samsung Epis Holdings) will not be constrained by potential conflicts of interest with CDMO customers; 
thus, it will have the flexibility to explore opportunities in novel drug development (in addition to biosimilars), providing long-term upside. 
• Ahead of the spin-off, potential catalysts include: 1) additional order wins with the start -up of Plant 5; and 2) the release of Plant 6 
investment plans.
• The firm signed a W740bn contract manufacturing contract in Apr., and on May 26, it announced that it had closed two addition al deals 
(totaling W440bn) with pharmaceutical companies based in Europe and Asia.
Source: Samsung Biologics, Mirae Asset Securities Research

Mirae Asset Securities Research6 | Mirae Asset Minutes
• The cosmetics sector reported strong 1Q25 results. Structurally growing segments such as indie beauty brands and ODMs performed well, 
and even legacy brands delivered solid results for the first time in a while.
• A key highlight was improving earnings in China (where expectations had been low). 
• After falling to 12x in 2H24 on peak growth concerns, the cosmetics sector’s 12-month forward P/E has recovered to 16x. However, it has 
yet to return to 20x—the level seen during the global expansion phase in 1H24.
• While the market has begun to price in near-term earnings improvement, we believe shares have yet to fully reflect the sector’s broader 
upside potential. As such, we see room for further valuation expansion.
Cosmetics | Songyi Bae   songyi.bae@miraeasset.com

Mirae Asset Securities Research7 | Mirae Asset Minutes
Cosmax   | Songyi Bae   songyi.bae@miraeasset.com
Note: Incl. Chinese joint venture
Source: Cosmax, Mirae Asset Securities Research
Source: Cosmax, Mirae Asset Securities Research
• Cosmax had initially planned to expand capacity by 30% over the course of 2025, but it pulled the timeline forward, completin g the 
expansion in 1Q25. With high-volume buyers secured, the added capacity positions the company for sharp growth. 
• The values of subsidiaries Cosmax Neo (packaging) and CM Tech (raw materials) have come into focus. In 1Q25, their combined O P 
exceeded W4bn, accounting for more than 8% of the consolidated figure, due to solid results from mass-market brands in overseas 
markets. Previously, these subsidiaries had made a minor contribution (annual OP of less than W10bn; less than 5% of consolid ated OP).
• In 1Q25, the China unit reported growth for the second straight quarter, and the Shanghai subsidiary returned to growth for t he first time 
in four quarters, signaling a recovery in market conditions. A broad-based order recovery is underway across both indie and legacy brands.
Cosmax: Capacity trend Cosmax: Subsidiary earnings (contribution rising meaningfully)

Entertainment   | Gyuyeon Kim gyuyeon.kim@miraeasset.com
Source: Mirae Asset Securities Research Source: Mirae Asset Securities Research
Earnings-driven rally taking shape Merch/licensing revenue catching up with music revenue
• The entertainment sector’s 12-month forward P/E has been climbing higher above 20x (amid a valuation recovery driven by turnaround 
momentum). In 2H25, a further rise to above 30x will likely require stronger earnings momentum. 
• We see multiple factors that could drive upward earnings forecast revisions in 2H25. In particular, the resumption of North A merican 
momentum—driven by major acts such as Stray Kids, BTS, and Blackpink—should reinforce the sector’s long-term growth story.
• The expansion of the merchandise customer base is also emerging as a structural growth driver. Merchandise is increasingly re aching 
beyond core fans, driven by character-based IP and goods designed for everyday use. As a result, concerts and licensing—key channels for 
driving merchandise sales—are playing an increasingly important role.
• If China reopens its concert market, this would serve as another structural growth driver.

• Short-term drivers: Aespa’s comeback, Dear U consolidation, and likely record earnings in 2Q25
- An earnings surprise is likely in 2Q25, backed by 10 new album releases and growing album sales by Riize and NCT Wish.
- Aespa’s comeback album could secure spots on major global charts, providing a valuation boost.
- Dear U is likely to report record earnings for 2Q25; China momentum should provide further upside. 
• Medium/long-term drivers: Aespa’s US potential and NCT Wish’s growth potential
- We forecast 2025 OP at W200.6bn (vs. consensus of W158bn) and 2026 OP at W230.7bn (vs. consensus of W187.1bn).
- If Aespa releases another hit, its concerts could increase in scale. Riize/NCT Wish should also contribute more to earnings going forward.

Mirae Asset Securities Research10 | Mirae Asset Minutes
Sector Analyst Sector comments Top picks Stock-specific comments
Energy Jinho Lee
- Renewables: Stocks have come under pressure 
following the US House’s passage of the budget 
reconciliation bill (OBBB); the bill proposes scaling 
back IRA subsidies via: 1) ITC/PTC cuts for solar/wind 
projects; 2) the removal of tax credit eligibility for TPO 
residential solar systems; 3) the phasing out of the 
AMPC from 2030; and 4) restrictions on IRA subsidies 
for FEOC-related firms starting in 2026
- Solar PV: If these provisions remain intact, Hanwha 
Solutions' residential solar business should see slower 
growth due to reduced subsidies for both TPO and 
loan-based systems; that said, the AMPC should 
remain in place for the time being, which is positive
- Wind: Wind subsidies under the AMPC would be 
reduced starting in 2028 (vs. 2030 for solar); while 
overall sentiment on wind is weak in the US, the stop 
work order for the Empire Wind offshore project was 
lifted, supporting a rebound in wind energy stocks
[Short term]
Hanwha 
Solutions
[Medium term]
Hanwha 
Solutions
Hanwha Solutions
- Investment points: 1) US solar module prices are likely to rise 
before/after AD/CVD implementation (Jun. 9); 2) FEOC rules 
will likely make it more difficult for Chinese solar modules to 
enter the US market; and 3) the AMPC looks likely to remain in 
place through 2031 (with a phase-out starting in 2030)
Oil Refining/
Chemicals Jinho Lee
- Oil refining: The outlook remains positive; with 
demand growth outpacing the net increase in refining 
capacity, supply/demand should remain tight through 
Nov. (40% of planned capacity additions are 
concentrated in Dec.)
- Chemicals: Tariff uncertainties are dampening 
demand for chemical products; that said, if crude 
remains in the US$50-60/bbl range for an extended 
period, domestic players’ cost competitiveness could 
improve
[Short term]
S-Oil
[Medium term]
S-Oil 
S-Oil
- Asian petroleum product prices could bounce back on a 
potential fall in low-priced oil exports from Russia and Iran; 
gasoline margins have recovered on decreased Chinese 
exports and the start of the driving season; attractive 
valuation (P/B of 0.8x)

Defense/
Aerospace
Dong-ho 
Jeong
- Korean defense firms posted solid 1Q25 results, with 
aggregate OP exceeding the consensus by 14.4%; OP 
estimates have been revised up by 8% for 2025 and 
14% for 2026; Hyundai Rotem, Hanwha Systems, and 
Hanwha Aerospace have high earnings visibility 
- The upcoming NATO summit (Jun. 24–25) should serve 
as a key catalyst; with discussions on European 
rearmament expected to take center stage, European 
defense stocks should continue to rally; the valuation 
gap between Korean and European defense stocks has 
narrowed to 28% (vs. 42% in April), and we believe this 
trend will continue
- We reiterate our Overweight call on the defense sector, 
given intensifying geopolitical risks and the 
accelerating global arms buildup; we recommend a 
selective investment approach, focusing on companies 
that are likely to enjoy solid earnings/order 
momentum in 2H25 and have room to further narrow 
the valuation gap with European peers.
[Short term] 
Hyundai Rotem 
[Medium term]
Hanwha 
Aerospace
Hyundai Rotem
- 1Q25 OP came in at W202.9bn (+354% YoY; 8.7% above the 
consensus); despite 1Q being the off-season, the defense 
solutions unit’s OP margin was strong at 29.5% (+15.2%p YoY, 
-3%p QoQ), driven by a higher share of exports and operating 
leverage effects from repeat production; we estimate the 
defense export margin at 39.1% (+17.5% YoY, -3.3% QoQ)
- Takeaways from the earnings call: 1) the factors behind the 
delay in the  Poland follow-up contract have been resolved; 2) 
there will be no revenue gap in 2H25; and 3) the defense 
export margin is expected to remain above 40% in 2Q-4Q25
- The potential export pipeline, which had been limited to 
Poland and Romania (300 units), has grown to include 
Slovakia (104 units), Peru (200 units), Saudi Arabia (700 units), 
Morocco (400 units), and India (1,770 units)
Hanwha Aerospace
- Hanwha Aerospace is set to raise W2.9tr (price set at 
W687,000); it plans to invest in overseas defense production 
capacity (W1.3tr; by 2028), overseas defense joint ventures 
(W0.9tr), other overseas projects (W3.2tr), and land systems 
infrastructure (W2.3tr)
- The company plans to invest W500bn–W1tr in cooperation 
with Saudi Arabia; of the rights offering proceeds, W418.8bn 
will be used to establish a joint venture with a local partner 
- In the US, Hanwha Aerospace plans to invest W600bn to build 
an MCS smart factory; if exports of 155mm shells and 
propellants to Europe and the US materialize, both revenue 
and profits should see a further boost, and the valuation gap 
with Rheinmetall should narrow

Mirae Asset Securities Research12 | Mirae Asset Minutes
Sector Analyst Sector comments Top picks Stock-specific comments
Shipbuilding Dong-ho 
Jeong 
- Shipbuilders posted strong 1Q25 earnings, with 
aggregate OP beating the consensus by 53.4%; we 
lifted our aggregate OP forecasts by 35% for 2025 and 
27% for 2026; HD HHI (our top pick) saw the largest 
upward OP forecast revisions
- We maintain our Overweight rating; price, volume, 
and cost factors all remain favorable (high 
prices/steady order flows).
- High pricing is likely to persist amid a global shortage 
in shipyard capacity and high replacement demand 
(due to aging and non-compliant vessels); with the 
lifting of regulatory (IMO/USTR) uncertainties, order 
momentum should resume in 2H25; naval export 
contract wins could drive further valuation upside 
(above historical levels)
- Aggregate OP projected to grow at a 2023-27 CAGR of 
95%; the current cycle supports a valuation premium 
(vs. past cycles)
- Focus on companies with strong 2H25 earnings 
momentum and exposure to the offshore, engine, and 
naval segments
[Short term]
HD HHI
[Medium term]
HD HHI
HD Hyundai Heavy Industries
- The stock remains a valid earnings play; of note, in 1Q25, HD 
Hyundai Samho and Hanwha Ocean delivered notable profit 
improvements on the back of methanol-fueled container ship 
deliveries and the first phase of the Qatar LNG carrier project; 
HD HHI should see similar profit growth, as it will begin 
delivering vessels of the same types in 2Q-3Q25
- New orders should resume in 2H25, as the finalization of the 
IMO carbon pricing scheme and USTR measures has helped 
lift uncertainty over shippers’ future fleet composition; as 
order backlogs grow, newbuilding prices should also rebound
- Global naval ship demand is on the rise; Romania recently 
proposed a partnership with HD HHI, while Bangladesh is 
reportedly seeking to acquire six submarines; other countries 
(e.g., the US) are pursuing naval ship procurement projects; if 
a major naval export deal is signed, the defense narrative 
could gain meaningful traction within the shipbuilding sector.
- HD HHI is currently trading at a 12-month forward P/E of 
23.8x, 12% higher than SHI (21.3x); while buying momentum 
could be affected by the stock’s investment warning 
designation, the recent correction should be viewed as a 
buying opportunity

Daewoo E&C
- Despite concerns over the absence of overseas order wins

Hyundai E&C
- We see positive momentum across the nuclear value chain, 
backed by: 1) growing expectations for global nuclear 
expansion; and 2) increased visibility on the Bulgarian nuclear 
EPC project and Palisades SMR project in the US 
- The stock is currently trading at a 2025F P/B of 0.71x; while a 
near-term pullback is possible following the recent rally, we 
see further upside to valuation due to the strong earnings 
outlook (2025 OP likely to exceed W1tr) and the ongoing 
expansion in overseas businesses (e.g., nuclear)
Steel Ki Ryong Kim
- China pledged to cut steel output by 50mn tonnes (out 
of 1bn tonnes produced last year) during its NPC in 
Mar., but the plan does not appear to have been 
executed yet; while there are few signs of supply 
tightening in China, supply/demand dynamics should 
still improve, as antidumping measures by other 
countries could limit Chinese exports
- Despite a seasonal demand uptick in Apr.-May, 
domestic steel prices in China have remained flat; but 
with raw material prices stabilizing lower, Chinese 
steelmakers’ spreads are holding steady MoM
- In the near term, we expect earnings to recover in 
2Q25 after bottoming in 1Q25; we believe upcoming 
preliminary rulings on antidumping cases targeting 
Chinese and Japanese hot-rolled coil (due in Jul.–Aug.) 
could serve as a key catalyst for the sector

POSCO Holdings
POSCO Holdings

- We expect margins to pick up on: 1) improvements in

Transportation Jay JH Ryu
- Shipping: The tariff reprieve drove a sharp WoW rise in 
the SCFI (+10% overall; +30% on US East Coast and 
+20% on US West Coast routes); this week, the index 
has continued rising (especially in Europe) amid 
concerns over reduced supply (+7.2% WoW overall; 
+14.1% on European routes and +5-6% on US routes)
- Hapag-Lloyd reported a 50% WoW surge in cargo 
bookings on China-US routes; market conditions 
should remain strong due to front-loaded exports and 
an additional general rate increase in Jun.
- Airlines: The USD/KRW has fallen to the lowest level in 
six months amid both dollar weakness and won 
strength (with Korea-US FX talks fueling further gains 
for the won); airlines are poised to benefit, as a lower 
USD/KRW should help improve passenger demand 
and reduce costs, leading to earnings improvements
- The Baltic Air Freight Index continued falling WoW; 
concerns persist over a potential drop in US-bound 
volumes from Chinese e-commerce companies 
(AliExpress, Temu, and Shein)

Medtech Choong-hyun 
Kim, CFA
- Aesthetic devices: The influx of foreign patients 
visiting Korea for dermatological procedures has led 
to particularly strong earnings growth for companies 
with original brands; premium global brands such as 
Ulthera and Thermage generate revenues several 
times higher than leading Korean names; foreign 
visitors are prioritizing brand recognition and 
discounts from list prices (over absolute costs); 
against this backdrop, owning a strong original 
brand is a major advantage; companies without solid 
original brands need to invest in building brand 
value (e.g., through clinical data, B2C marketing, the 
development of new procedures, etc.)
- Diagnostics: Leading diagnostics players delivered 
OP turnarounds in 1Q25, fueling expectations for 
earnings growth going forward; while thematic 
interest in infectious diseases is re-emerging due to 
outbreaks in neighboring countries, the real focus 
should be on improving fundamentals

Global Biotech Mihwa Seo 
- In an executive order, the Trump administration 
announced plans to implement a most-favored-nation 
drug pricing model, which would link US prices to the 
lowest levels paid by OECD countries with per-capita 
GDPs of at least 60% of that of the US; for companies 
that market drugs in the US, this has created 
uncertainty over potential price cuts
- For new drug developers, uncertainty is also rising 
around drug approval timelines; the FDA is informing 
a growing number of companies that PDUFA 
deadlines may not be met; even companies that were 
expecting imminent approvals could face delays

growth; defending capital/minimizing risk will likely 
remain the priority

Semiconductors Young-gun 
Kim
- AI-related momentum has weakened with the end of 
Computex 2025 and other catalysts; however, Nvidia’s 
upcoming earnings release could serve as a new driver
- Nvidia’s allocation issues suggest that demand is far 
outpacing supply; while this points to healthy underlying 
demand, margin improvement remains limited, making 
it unclear how the market will interpret the current 
supply/demand imbalance 
- Contract prices for conventional memory chips surged 
over 20% due to preemptive orders ahead of US tariffs 
and the market perception that prices have bottomed; 
while it is unclear whether this price rally will continue 
through year-end (as it does not reflect fundamental 
demand improvement), it is positive that channel 
inventories are normalizing
- The lack of clear upward revisions in shipment/sales 
forecasts for end-products (smartphones, PCs, etc.) 
suggests price momentum could be short-lived
- That said, we see some structural demand drivers that 
could sustain price growth, including: 1) the upcoming 
end of Windows 10 support (likely to trigger a PC 
replacement cycle); 2) solid demand for HBM; and 3) the 
trend toward higher-capacity enterprise SSDs

Samsung Electronics 
- Undervalued at a P/B of 0.9x; our SOTP-based target price 
(W80,000) implies a 2025F P/E of 12x and 2025F P/B of 1.2x,

suppliers, securing certification could provide a short-term 
sentiment boost and strengthen long-term fundamentals

- Low valuation (2025F P/E of 18x; bottom of range since 2016)
- NAVER Plus Store (separate commerce app; 70,000 daily 
downloads) should serve as another upside catalyst for 
shares
- The app currently has around 5mn MAUs, and we expect the 
figure to reach 10mn by year-end
- The commission rate for Smart Store sellers is likely to 
increase by 1%p in Jun., boosting annual profits by around 
W300bn
- Compared to Google, declining search queries are less of a 
concern for NAVER, as more than 80% of user time on the 
platform is spent on vertical services
Games HeeSeok Lim
- Companies that are nimbly adapting to the industry-
wide trend of declining player engagement should see 
their valuations re-rate higher; these include Krafton in 
the shooter genre and Shift Up and Nexon Games in the 
subculture genre
- Netmarble is poised to benefit from app store 
commission cuts and thus also deserves continued 
attention
- Investors should also monitor companies with major 
new releases scheduled for this year, including NCsoft 
(Aion 2) and Netmarble (The Seven Deadly Sins: Origin)
[Short term]
Shift Up 
[Medium term]
Shift Up
Shift Up
- Goddess of Victory: Nikke was launched in China on May 22; 
its early iOS revenue ranking has fallen short of expectations, 
prompting a share price correction; however, its 
performance is broadly in line with expectations when 
factoring in its strong showing on Chinese platforms and PC; 
we continue to expect the title to generate average daily 
revenue of W1bn in China in 2025 
- We see potential for a boost in player spending once “pickup 
character” recruitment events (the game’s core monetization 
feature) begin in China
- For Stellar Blade, both a PC release and a crossover with 
Goddess of Victory: Nikke are scheduled for Jun. 
- The title’s PC sales are expected to exceed its console sales 
(cumulative console sales estimated at over 2mn units)

Sector Analyst Sector comments Top picks Stock-specific comments
Telecom Services Soojin Kim
- The investigation into the USIM data breach at SKT is 
underway, with final findings and potential fines 
expected to be announced by end-Jun.
- While shares of KT and LG Uplus have gained since the 
incident, they are still trading at a discount to global 
peers
[Short term]
LG Uplus 
[Medium term]
LG Uplus
LG Uplus
- The firm announced that it will continue to conduct share 
buybacks/cancellations; foreign ownership stands at around 
36% (well below the limit)
- The stock has the lowest valuation among the three major 
telcos (12MF EV/EBITDA of 3.1x)
IT Services Soojin Kim
- Following 1Q25 earnings releases, concerns over 
potential cuts in IT spending have eased, boosting 
expectations for earnings surprises in 2H25
- The commercialization of AI agents should begin in 
earnest in 2H25, driving positive momentum for the 
sector
[Short term]
LG CNS
[Medium term]
LG CNS
LG CNS 
- The firm is demonstrating some of the most notable AI-
related achievements in Korea (e.g., launching a ChatGPT-
based enterprise AI service for Shinhan Bank and 
introducing an AI-powered ERP solution for SAP 
environments)
- While the scheduled expiration of the six-month lock-up 
period (for major shareholders) in early Aug. should cap 
short-term upside, the stock’s undemanding valuation could 
still lead to some near-term gains

As of May 12, 2025, the Trading Buy rating category has been removed from our investment rating system. 
Stocks expected to deliver a 12-month return between +10% and less than +20% may be rated either Buy or Hold at the discretion of the research analyst.

Kakaopay as underlying assets; other than this, Mirae Asset Securities Co., Ltd. has no special interests in the covered companies.

As of the publication date, Mirae Asset Securities Co., Ltd. is acting as a financial advisor to POSCO Holdings, LigaChem Biosciences, and Daewoo E&C for their share buybacks/cancellations. 
As of the publication date, Mirae Asset Securities Co., Ltd. provides services for HD Hyundai Heavy Industries to ensure the fulfillment of its debt obligations, including payment guarantees, endorsement of notes, collateralization, and debt assumptions.
